subject.title: [Bug]: Enabling Codex plugin causes Runtime to switch to OpenAI Codex and ignore configured primary model, resulting in GPT-5.4-nano TPM failures

question: Should this issue be handled as a concrete reproduction under the open session model/auth resolver work, or as a narrower Codex plugin runtime-selection bug?
rationale: The reporter's later `/model openai/gpt-5.4-nano` clarification makes the product contract ambiguous: OpenAI-selected sessions currently use Codex by documented default, but the user-visible status and primary-model expectations remain confusing and may share the resolver root cause.

options.title: Keep open under resolver work
options.body: Track this issue as a concrete DeepSeek-plus-Codex-plugin reproduction while the shared session model/runtime resolver is repaired.

options.title: Close into the canonical resolver tracker
options.body: Close this issue as a duplicate after preserving the Feishu, screenshot, and `/model` clarification evidence on the open resolver tracker.

options.title: Make Codex opt-in for existing OpenAI session overrides
options.body: Change runtime selection so enabling the Codex plugin does not affect already selected OpenAI sessions unless maintainers intentionally change the documented default.

recommendation.title: Keep open under resolver work
recommendation.body: Track this issue as a concrete DeepSeek-plus-Codex-plugin reproduction while the shared session model/runtime resolver is repaired.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest current code ownership trail runs through OpenAI/Codex routing and harness policy changes.
